Hazel Bramblecap.narrative: I keep the hollow's salve store, and I walk the old forest paths to Tanglewood for the herbs I cannot grow in my own rows. My aunt Pipwort is Eldest, and I am her niece, which means the hollow watches me more closely than it watches most. I have been paying the Tanglewood healer in salves for a winter's worth of roots and I have not paid enough, and the salve jars on my shelf are getting light. I tend the elders and dose the children, and I want the hollow to name who follows Pipwort openly, before the root table splits over it.
goals: settle the Tanglewood debt before the salve store runs dry
see Pipwort name her successor openly
keep the winter cough from the elders

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: She raised me in the salve shed; I want her to speak before it is too late.

relations.name: Sorrel Bramblecap
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He grumbles at the giants' track and I let him; he is steady where I fret.

relations.name: Tamarisk Bramblecap
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She gathers berries at my heel and knows the salve jars by smell.

relations.name: Betony Mossfoot
relations.label: friend
relations.note: The best hand with a fever in the hollow; we share what we know.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She assumes the memory will be hers; I say nothing to her face.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: kinswoman by marriage
relations.note: Years beside Pipwort with the seed store; she has a claim too.

relations.name: Ysolde Fenwick
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: The Tanglewood healer; her word came cold and I have no answer yet.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: the hollow's cook
relations.note: She feeds us all at the common table and asks after my jars.

memories.gist: Pipwort set the salve jars in my hands when I was a girl and told me the hollow's ills were mine now.
The winter the cough went through the hollow, Betony and I sat up three nights with the elders and lost only one.
I walked to Tanglewood through wet leaves and came home with roots and a promise to pay in salves.
Sorrel brought in the first barley from the grain patch and I cooked it at the common table for everyone.
Tamarisk asked me why the jars were half empty and I had no good answer for a child.

stances.why: The healer's roots kept the hollow alive last winter; I will not pretend I owe nothing.
A quarrel over Pipwort's memory would split the root table worse than any choice made in daylight.
I dose the elders and the children alike and take no mark for it.
The plants I need grow in the deep shade; cut it and the salves go with it.

Hazel Bramblecap.secret: I have been quietly watering the salves I give the healer to make them stretch, and if she finds out she will trust nothing I send.

Sorrel Bramblecap.narrative: I work the hollow's grain patch and the berry rows, and I carry the surplus to the Ferncross woodcutters for what we cannot grow. My wife Hazel keeps the salve store and frets over her jars; I keep my grumbles to the giants' track, which takes our timber and gives us little. I want a second strip by the stream, and I have asked the Eldest for it more than once. The hollow is small and the winter is long, and I would rather be planting than talking.
goals: win a second strip by the stream
bring in a good berry harvest for Ferncross
see the salve store refilled before the coughs come

relations.name: Hazel Bramblecap
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She frets and I plant; between us the house holds.

relations.name: Tamarisk Bramblecap
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She picks the rows clean and I let her eat as she goes.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: aunt by marriage
relations.note: She has not given me the stream strip yet, and I have asked plainly.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: seed-keeper
relations.note: She knows which seed will take to the poor ground; I go to her before I sow.

relations.name: Bramwell Ashdown
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: He takes my berries at Ferncross and pays fair enough.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: kinswoman
relations.note: She feeds us all; I eat at her table and say little.

relations.name: Yarrow Underbank
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He will not fell a living tree, and I will not ask him to.

memories.gist: The Lean Year blight came through the berry rows and I burned what I could not save.
Hazel and I planted the grain patch together the spring after, and it came up thick.
I carried a full pack of berries to Ferncross and came back with a new axe head and a sack of salt.
A giant's track runs above our rows and their timber haul tears the bank when the rains come.
Tamarisk was born in the house by the berry rows and Hazel would not let me in until the sun rose.

stances.why: A hollow that eats in winter can argue all it likes in spring.
I have no claim either way, but I want it settled before the rows are sown.
Their sledges cut our bank and we see none of the timber.
The stream strip is poor but it is ours to try, and I would rather try than wait.

Sorrel Bramblecap.secret: I have been taking a handful of the common grain each week and hiding it in the loft against a bad winter, and I have not told Hazel.

Tamarisk Bramblecap.narrative: I gather berries in the rows with my father and follow my mother to the salve shed, where the jars smell of green and bitter things. I play with Rush Fenwick by the garden paths and I know which flowers are good for a cough. The deep caves in the hills frighten me, and I do not like to be out when the light goes.
goals: fill my basket before my father does
learn the name of every flower

relations.name: Hazel Bramblecap
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She lets me hold the jars if I am careful.

relations.name: Sorrel Bramblecap
relations.label: father
relations.note: He lifts me over the berry rows and lets me eat as I pick.

relations.name: Rush Fenwick
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play by the garden paths and she knows the smoke shed.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: great-aunt
relations.note: She is very old and smells of the seed store, and she pats my head.

memories.gist: I ate so many berries my mouth went purple and my mother laughed at me.
A big folk came up the track with a sledge and I hid behind my father's legs.
